text:
alisha: heads-up — staging CI perf alarm after last night's merges. p99 token path latency ~3x on small-chat workload. saw a spike right after model-bump + kernel-selector tune merge. @marc can you take a look?
marc: digging in now. I see batching oscillation traces and a big chunk of time in kernel selection fallback. suspecting prefetch affinity flip from PR #4219.
vikas: I ran a quick `perf` on a repro trace — KV cache miss rate jumps ~40% after the bump, and batch scheduler shows more frequent tiny batches (n=1-3).
nina: confirming on canary: flamegraph -> top frames are kernel_selector::choose_variant and kv_cache::lookup. link: https://perf.redwood/team/flame/353987 (private) :eyes:
perf-bot: CI perf regression detected: p99_latency +210% (baseline 48ms -> 155ms). Regression window: 2026-03-16 02:12 -> 2026-03-16 02:18. Suspected commits: 7f3a2c1, 9b4d8e0
james: I ran a git-bisect locally across last 12 merges. The change that reproduces is the kernel-selector heuristic that prefers single-stream affinity for models with avg_seq_len < 32 (introduced in 9b4d8e0).
alisha: interesting — but why would that cause KV misses? The tokenizer bump changed tokenization boundaries for conversational inputs, increasing average seq length by ~10-15% for that workload. that could flip pathing.
marc: exactly — tokenizer config drift + the new affinity rule means requests that used to route to multi-stream kernel now go to single-stream optimized kernels with smaller KV cache allocation, causing frequent evictions. KV thrash explains the batch oscillation (jobs wait for cache warmup).
vikas: repro script: ```bash
# reproduce p99 locally
python tools/repro_perf.py --trace small_chat.json --model v4.1-onboard
# compare selector outputs
python tools/inspect_selector.py --trace small_chat.json --commit 9b4d8e0
```
nina: can confirm patching kernel-selector to fall back to multi-stream when kv_hit_rate < 0.8 reduces p99 from 155ms -> 62ms on staging. created a quick patch: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4223
alisha: thanks. plan: hold the rollout, revert the heuristic commit if we don't get an out-of-band fix asap. @ci-bot can we enqueue a perf CI run for the PR 4223 on staging?
ci-bot: Enqueued perf job #7721 for PR 4223 on staging. ETA ~12m.
marc: also adding a short-term mitigation: pin tokenizer config for the canary to previous token-mapping (v4.0-tokenizer) while we validate selector change. avoids churn.
james: note for postmortem: we need a guardrail test in premerge perf that synthesizes tokenization distribution shifts when model onboards. adding to backlog.
perf-bot: perf job #7721 complete: p99 reduced to 60ms, p50 unaffected. Regression resolved in candidate PR 4223.
alisha: great. rollout paused -> canary kept at 0% until we land 4223 + pin. thanks everyone. I'll file a quick incident note and schedule a short postmortem with action items (selector guard, tokenizer-onboard test, KV warmup metrics). :thumbsup:
